# Research Memory Mutation Corpus

The quarantine gate builds its adversarial corpus in memory. No generated attack
payload is a product input or a checked-in benchmark result.

The frozen construction rule is ten families with 30 deterministic members each:

1. resource ceilings: total bytes, strings, event count, artifact count, item count,
   and nesting depth;
2. wire encodings: invalid UTF-8, BOM, duplicate keys, non-NFC text, lone surrogate,
   and JSON trailing polyglots;
3. closed schemas: schema/profile/version drift, unknown fields, artifact/event kinds,
   and Research OS enum drift;
4. identities: declared head, event/body/previous hashes, artifact IDs, semantic and
   storage digests, and canonical-body mutation;
5. history: sequence gaps, duplicates, reorder, forks, truncation, and cross-project
   replay;
6. references: missing/duplicate/unresolved subjects, snapshot self/wrong-kind/missing
   references, and wrong artifact identity metadata;
7. forged authority: malformed `user_confirmed`, passport identity, event/source
   identity, route fields, and self-signature claims;
8. authority-bearing fields: path, URL, command, tool, worker, persistence, execution,
   plugin, process, browser, SQL, network, and related variants;
9. freshness: 15 dataset-fingerprint mismatches and 15 stale Method Space/ruleset
   identities;
10. sensitive/polyglot formats: local rich text, SQLite and ZIP signatures, concatenated
    JSON, comments, NUL suffixes, trailing commas, and BOM.

Every member must be rejected or held with its predeclared closed reason, return zero
assertions, and retain a distinct case name. The test requires exactly 300 cases and
never writes generated bytes to disk.
